name: tap_pinger
describe: has a tap-activated ability that deals damage (repeatable pinger)
counterexample: Lightning Bolt - one-shot SP burn, no activated tap cost

name: phase_engine
describe: generates recurring value from beginning-of-phase triggers
counterexample: Giant Growth - one-shot SP pump, no Phase trigger

name: cost_reducer
describe: makes spells cheaper to cast via a static cost-reduction effect
counterexample: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben — her only static node is Mode$ RaiseCost (taxes noncreature spells {1} more), the structural mirror of a discount; the detector requires static mode ReduceCost, so she does not match (verified against the dataset).
strategic_note: Cost reducers are enablers like mana amplifiers: they generate no advantage alone, only when the deck casts what they discount. The ValidCard param partitions the 515-card cluster into two strategic tiers: 268 are Card.Self self-discounts (situational rate improvements on one spell, weak as deck glue) while the rest are deck-wide family discounts (Instant,Sorcery x27, any Card x29, Creature x17, plus color/tribe medallion variants). For sharper per-card recommendations, read the node's ValidCard and pair with that exact spell family; the generic complements chosen scale with any discount — SpellCast trigger payoffs (magecraft/Adeliz) convert extra casts per turn into value, Storm/ThisTurnCast counters (Aeve, Arclight Phoenix) count the additional spells a discount enables, and big generic-cost nonland cards capture the largest absolute mana savings.

name: buffs_attached
describe: grants +X/+X to the creature it's attached to (aura/equipment suit-up, not a global anthem)
counterexample: Glorious Anthem - has a Continuous static with AddPower+AddToughness, but its Affected is "Creature.YouCtrl" (a global anthem over your whole board, the tribal_lord/anthem family), not an EnchantedBy/AttachedBy attached target; verified the detector rejects it.
strategic_note: Voltron pattern: stacks stats onto one (ideally evasive or hexproof) creature, so it trades card economy for threat density and is 2-for-1'd by spot removal — hexproof carriers mitigate that, enchantress engines (SpellCast-Enchantment-to-Draw triggers) refund the cards, and becomes-attached triggers (Bramble Elemental, Siona, Eriette) convert each suit-up into extra value. Distinct from tribal_lord anthems, which spread +1/+1 wide over a YouCtrl-filtered board; detector separates the two on the Affected filter (EnchantedBy/AttachedBy vs YouCtrl). Pool selectivity 1.2% (408/34519).

name: mass_keyword_granter
describe: continuously grants keyword abilities (haste, flying, vigilance, etc.) to your whole team
counterexample: Glorious Anthem - its Continuous static affects Creature.YouCtrl but only carries AddPower/AddToughness with no AddKeyword param; it is a stat anthem, not a keyword granter (verified: detector returns False)
strategic_note: A single permanent multiplies across every body you control, so value scales linearly with board width: token swarms (Krenko, Raise the Alarm) turn one haste/evasion grant into N immediate or unblockable attackers, and attack/combat-damage trigger payoffs (Hellrider, Coastal Piracy, Edric) need exactly what these grant - haste to trigger now, evasion to connect. The effect is concentrated in one enchantment/artifact/creature, so it folds to targeted removal; decks leaning on it want redundancy or protection statics.

name: evasion_static
describe: carries or grants a can't-be-blocked / blocking-restriction static (CantBlockBy)
counterexample: Wind Drake - evasion via the Flying keyword only (kind K node); no CantBlockBy static node, so keyword-evasion stays a separate facet
strategic_note: CantBlockBy statics guarantee combat damage connects, so they convert saboteur bodies (DamageDone-to-player triggers like Thieving Magpie/Ohran Frostfang, 776 in pool) and attack triggers (1850 in pool) into reliable engines; power anthems (113 in pool) scale the unblocked hit. Detector matched 362/34519 records (1.05%) and passed the full validate_concept gate (ok=True, no errors); note the family also contains blocking-restriction variants (Air Bladder 'can block only creatures with flying') that share the same node shape.

name: cda_statline
describe: creature whose power/toughness are characteristic-defining (set equal to a counted quantity like creatures, lands, or cards in a zone)
counterexample: Godhead of Awe - its Continuous static also carries SetPower/SetToughness but with Affected=Creature.Other and no CharacteristicDefining flag: it rewrites OTHER creatures' stats to 1/1 rather than defining its own P/T from a counted quantity
strategic_note: These creatures are typically undercosted for their potential stats because the stats are earned: power equals a count (creatures you control, lands, graveyard cards, cards in hand). Build around them with complements that inflate the counted quantity (mill for graveyard-counters, token producers for board-counters, extra land drops for land-counters). Structural weakness: as layer-7a characteristic-defining abilities they are nullified by ability-removal effects like Dress Down or Humility, which drop them to base 0/0 and can kill them outright; they also shrink if the counted resource is exiled or swept.

name: recurring_forced_sacrifice
describe: forces sacrifices on a recurring phase trigger (upkeep/end step) - stax engines taxing each player's board (Anowon, Braids, Smokestack) and self-sacrificing drawback permanents (Arc Runner)
counterexample: Grave Pact - it chains to a Sacrifice API node, but from a ChangesZone (dies) trigger rather than a Phase trigger, so trigger_mode=Phase rejects it (verified non-matching; Magus of the Abyss also verified: Phase upkeep trigger but chains to Destroy, not Sacrifice)
strategic_note: The hint's pure-stax reading fails verification: 2 of 3 given examples (Anurid Scavenger, Arc Runner) are self-drawback sacrifices with no SacValid/Defined targeting other players. The stax/drawback split lives in the Sacrifice node's params (Defined: Player/TriggeredPlayer + SacValid = stax; bare DB:Sacrifice or UnlessCost = self-drawback), which the allowed detect primitives cannot express - a future param-aware primitive could split this into recurring_sacrifice_stax vs upkeep_drawback. The chosen complements serve both readings: token makers break symmetric-sacrifice parity (feed Smokestack/Braids with free bodies), death-trigger payoffs (Blood Artist) convert every forced creature sacrifice into drain, and graveyard recursion (Sun Titan) rebuys whatever the engine eats. Dataset-wide the detector fires on 215 faces vs 97 uncovered, so it also claims already-covered neighbors - acceptable for a hook, dedupe happens at registry level.

name: alternative_cost
describe: can be cast for an alternative cost instead of its mana cost (Force-family pitch costs, Daze-style bounce costs, conditional free casts)
counterexample: Counterspell - it must be cast for its printed {U}{U} mana cost and has no S-node with Mode AlternativeCost, so the detector rejects it; likewise Fury's free cast is the Evoke keyword node, not this static, and is correctly excluded.
strategic_note: These spells pay cards (pitch/exile/bounce/life) instead of mana, so they answer threats while fully tapped out and interact with taxes differently than normal spells: since the mana cost is never paid, mana-cost-shaped hate lands askew, but S:CantBeCast statics still stop them cold because they are still cast — hate against this family must forbid casting, not tax it. The card cost means each pitch is card disadvantage, so pair them with draw engines (hand_refill_engines), turn the free timing into extra prowess/magecraft/storm triggers (spell_cast_payoffs), and where the alternative cost discards, feed Discarded-mode payoffs (discard_payoffs).

name: amplifies_damage
describe: increases damage dealt via a replacement effect (deals double/triple/that much plus N instead)
counterexample: Divine Presence - it carries the exact same R node shell (Event$ DamageDone with a ReplaceWith), but its replacement (SVar Dmg3, VarValue 3) CAPS damage at 3 instead of amplifying it - it is a damage-reduction card, the mechanical opposite of this concept. Verified rejected by the detector, along with prevention (Battletide Alchemist, ReplaceWith DBReplace -> ReplaceDamage) and redirection (Pariah, ReplaceWith DmgEnchanted).
strategic_note: The R:DamageDone->replace signature is a mixed bag of 4 subfamilies; grounding in the scripts showed amplification is dominant (53 of 146 dataset-wide R:DamageDone replacements resolve to ReplaceCount$DamageAmount/Twice|Thrice|Plus.N, vs 27 prevention, ~30 damage-to-counters conversion, and small redirect/convert groups). Since the replace_with primitive only substring-matches the SVar name, the detector keys on the Forge naming convention (DmgTwice/DmgPlus*/DmgTriple/DamageReplace), which cleanly separates amplifiers from preventers/redirectors: 50 matched cards, zero observed false positives; it deliberately skips the ambiguous name Dmg3 (used by both Fiery Emancipation, an amplifier, and Divine Presence, a cap), trading 1-2 cards of recall for precision. Complements verified non-empty: burn_spells (652), ping_engines (520, repeatable activated DealDamage that turns doubling into an engine), damage_payoffs (866, T:DamageDone triggers whose 'that much' effects scale with amplified damage). The remaining prevention/conversion subfamilies deserve their own separate concept (e.g. prevents_damage) rather than being lumped in here.
